summary: Carlo Jamelle Harris is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned his Master of Arts in Philosophy at National Chengchi University, where he studied under Chen-kuo Lin.

Carmen Blacker (1924–2009) was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied at SOAS, Somerville College, Keio University, and under Shigeru Gorai. She held posts at the University of Cambridge from 1955 and served as president of the Folklore Society (1982–1984).

Carmen Dragonetti (1937–2018) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy after studying at the National University of San Marcos (~1958–1964). She held posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, the Nyingma Institute, and the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas.

Carmen Meinert is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who earned her PhD from the University of Bonn by 2001. She was a research fellow at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008) and Principal Investigator at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2019).

Carol A. Breckenridge (1942–2009) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1976) and held a post at the University of Chicago (~1982–1999).

Carol S. Anderson, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, completed her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under John A. Brinkman and W. S. Karunatillake. She served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College (attested 2004).

Carola Roloff (born 1959) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Geshe Thubten Ngawang, holding posts at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and University of Hamburg.
Carola S. Carstens specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctorate at the University of Hamburg by 2005 and held a post at Rice University from 1998 to 1999.
Carole M. Cusack (born 1962) is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Sydney from 1988 to 1995 and held a post there in 2013.

Carole McGranahan (born 1969) is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at Colgate University and the University of Michigan, with supervisors including Nicholas Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler, and took up posts at the University of Colorado around 2001.

Caroline Humphrey (born 1943) works in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She studied at Cambridge (under Edmund Leach) and Leeds, holding long-term academic posts at the University of Cambridge (1971–2010), Girton College, King's College, and the Scott Polar Research Institute.

Caroline Rhys Davids (1857–1942) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at University College London under George Croom Robertson, Reinhold Rost, and T. W. Rhys Davids, she held posts at the Pali Text Society, Manchester, and SOAS.

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington, serving there as a Graduate Teaching Associate and as a Visiting Lecturer at Denison University (attested 1990).
Carson Schütze (born 1968) is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, in 1997.

Catherine Bell (1954–2008) was a religious studies scholar and Sinologist. She studied under Joseph M. Kitagawa at the University of Chicago Divinity School (~1976–1983) and served as Bernard J. Hanley Professor of Religious Studies at Santa Clara University (1985–2008).

Catherine Cornille (born 1961) works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at KU Leuven (~1979–1989) and the University of Hawaiʻi (~1983–1985), and held a post as Associate Professor of Comparative Theology at Boston College (attested ~2005).

Catherine Elaine Prueitt specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the University of Rochester and completed her PhD at Emory University by 2016, where she studied under Laurie L. Patton and doctoral supervisor John D. Dunne.

Catherine Ella Blanshard Asher (1946–2023) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She received her PhD from the University of Minnesota by 1984, where she served as an assistant professor from ~1986 to 2021.

Catherine Ludvik is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. She earned her PhD at the University of Toronto under David Waterhouse and held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies, Hanazono, Stanford, Doshisha, and Kyoto Sangyo.
Cathy Cantwell (born 1900) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Kent by 1989 and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.
